title: Mechanically Robust, Durable, and Multifunctional Hyper-Crosslinked Elastomer Based on Metal–Organic-Cluster Crosslinker: The Role of Topological Structure

material_class.structural_family: Tb9 β-diketonate metal–organic cluster with polymerizable vinyl groups

synthesis.procedure: Under argon, 5 g (0.035 mol) (2-propenyl) 3-oxobutanoate was dissolved in 10 mL THF. 3.98 g (8.75 mmol) Tb(NO3)3·6H2O was dissolved in 10 mL EtOH and dropped into the ligand solution. After 4 h, 5 mL triethylamine was added and the mixture was reacted for another 2 h. The solution was allowed to volatilize slowly for three days. The resulting colorless crystals were washed several times with deionized water and vacuum-dried at 60 °C (5.54 g, 71%).
synthesis.temperature: not specified for the coordination steps; vacuum drying at 60 °C
synthesis.time: 4 h coordination, then 2 h after adding triethylamine; slow volatilization for 3 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution coordination under argon followed by slow solvent volatilization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow volatilization for three days; crystals washed with deionized water several times and vacuum-dried at 60 °C

properties.summary: Colorless crystals. UV–vis absorption of MOC in solution is shifted to 275 nm relative to the free β-diketone ligand (264 nm), attributed to conjugation upon Tb(III) coordination. Subsequent polymer networks made from this cluster show Tb3+ 5D4→7FJ emission and higher quantum yield than a conventional coordination network, but those data belong to the elastomer films rather than the isolated cluster.

measurements.name: UV–vis absorption maximum
measurements.conditions: MOC in solution; compared with free (2-propenyl) 3-oxobutanoate at 264 nm and Tb-ptd at 286 nm (Figure 1C)
